picks.title: Odyssey-3 is a new generative world model that you can try for free
picks.excerpt: Odyssey released its 14-billion-parameter world model Odyssey-3 as a public research preview. It generates interactive environments from text prompts in real time.
picks.rationale: Fresh release: a free, real-time text-to-interactive-environment world model designers can try today for spatial and scene ideation.

picks.title: Context Libraries: How AI power users manage context engineering
picks.excerpt: NN/g research finds Claude power users rarely edit their context files and often can't find them. Your AI agent is only as powerful as its context library.
picks.rationale: Original NN/g user research on how people manage AI context files. It works as a workflow tip for designers and also shows a UX gap for teams building agent tools.

picks.title: Tesler's Law: complexity moved to a different part of the journey
picks.excerpt: AI did not remove the complexity of software; it removed the interface that told you where the complexity went. Applies Tesler's Law of conservation of complexity to chat-field AI products.
picks.rationale: Applies a classic UX law to chat-first AI products, giving designers a concrete lens for where complexity lands in the journey.

picks.title: AI-generated UI is fast design, not UX
picks.excerpt: An editor's pick arguing that AI-generated interfaces speed up production but skip problem discovery, and making the case for wandering and craft in the age of AI.
picks.rationale: Replacement for the Robot Report advertorial. It is a process argument about where AI UI generation fits in the design workflow (production, not discovery), so it is filed under workflow rather than as a third Figma card.

picks.title: Why 'boring' AI is Hollywood's best bet
picks.excerpt: Generative AI could be the film industry's secret weapon, but not in the way people expect: the real wins are in unglamorous production and VFX pipeline tasks.
picks.rationale: Shows visual and VFX artists where generative AI actually pays off: unglamorous pre-production and pipeline tasks, not headline generation. The author is Filmustage's CEO, but the piece is genuinely about AI pre-production, so it stays.
